args.text: When the description states a specific event or activity, use a BPMN label that preserves its meaning and explicitly stated details rather than a generic or narrower label.

trace.reason: Check whether documented guidance already covers faithful, semantically precise BPMN labels.

result.rule: When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Create reusable bpmn:message elements and messageRef only when communication content or shared message identity matters.
For a message event, put messageRef on its bpmn:messageEventDefinition, never on the event element itself.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.

args.text: When the description states a meaningful event outcome or trigger, use a faithful BPMN label that preserves it rather than a generic label.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing learned guideline already covers meaningful event labels before selecting the best-supported rule.

result.rule: When the description states a meaningful object, recipient, or responsible role for an activity: Use a concise BPMN label that preserves the described action and those details when they distinguish or clarify the activity.

When the description explicitly states what triggers the process or what outcome terminates it: Label the corresponding start or end event with a concise, faithful description of that stated trigger or outcome rather than a generic label.

When the description states multiple possible actions or outcomes for a single activity: Label the corresponding BPMN activity so that each explicitly stated alternative remains visible; do not use a narrower label that omits one.
When the description explicitly states the object or scope of an activity: Retain that meaningful object or scope in the BPMN task label while keeping the label concise.

args.text: When the description states a meaningful trigger for starting a process or an outcome for ending it, label the corresponding start or end event with a concise description that preserves that meaning rather than using a generic label.

trace.reason: Verify that the event-label guideline is general and not tied to this process.
